questions.q: State the law of demand and explain the law of diminishing marginal utility that underlies it.

answer.text: The law of demand states that, other things remaining equal, the quantity of a good that a consumer buys rises when its price falls, and falls when its price rises. There is thus an inverse relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded, which is why the demand curve slopes downward from left to right.

This behaviour is explained by the law of diminishing marginal utility. Marginal utility is the extra satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming one more unit of a good. As a person consumes more and more of a good, the satisfaction from each additional unit becomes smaller. So a consumer is willing to buy extra units only if the price falls to match the lower satisfaction they give.
A consumer buys a good up to the point where its marginal utility equals its price.

answer: Thus diminishing marginal utility explains why consumers buy more only at lower prices, giving us the law of demand.
